e: Under the shared responsibility model, the customer creates and configures RDS DB instances (including the maintenance window), manages software on the ECS hosts (monitoring, patching, logging, intrusion detection), and encrypts data in transit over Direct Connect. AWS manages the RDS infrastructure, OS, engine patching, and physical security.

The job runs for 10 seconds once an hour and needs 1 GB of memory, which fits a Lambda function with 1 GB memory triggered by an EventBridge schedule, so the company pays only for the seconds used. Fargate or EC2 options cost more for an idle workload.

AWS Backup supports both EC2 and S3, and a vault lock in compliance mode makes backups immutable for the retention period so nobody (including the root user) can alter or delete them. Governance mode can be overridden by authorized users, and DLM and File Gateway don't provide WORM protection.

Workload Discovery on AWS automatically discovers resources across accounts and Regions and builds interactive architecture diagrams with relationships between them. Systems Manager Inventory, manual diagrams, or X-Ray don't map relationships across accounts.

Create the budget in AWS Budgets (Billing dashboard) per account, create an IAM role that AWS Budgets can assume to run budget actions, and add an alert plus a budget action that applies an SCP to stop further provisioning when the threshold is reached. IAM users can't be used for budget actions, and Config rules don't prevent provisioning.

AWS Backup centrally manages backup plans and cross-Region copies of EC2 backups from one account, at lower cost than running a duplicate DR environment, and the instances can be restored in the second Region when needed. A standing duplicate environment or DataSync would cost more.

AWS Transfer Family supports the AS2 protocol, and a custom identity provider can be integrated through a Lambda function (or API Gateway) for authentication. DataSync, AppFlow, and Storage Gateway don't support AS2.

Lambda (up to 10 GB memory and 10 GB ephemeral storage) behind API Gateway runs the computation without servers, and RDS provides the relational data store with managed administration. EC2 and EKS need more management, and DynamoDB isn't relational.

Department tags are user-defined, and cost allocation tags must be activated in the Organizations management account's billing console so that they apply across all accounts. Then one Cost Explorer report grouped by the tag and filtered by EC2 shows spending by department. AWS-defined tags don't include a custom department tag, and member accounts can't activate them organization-wide.

Amazon AppFlow is a managed integration service with a native Salesforce connector that transfers data to S3 securely, encrypts data in transit, and supports KMS customer managed keys for data at rest, with no code. Lambda, Step Functions, or a custom connector require building and maintaining the integration.

Global Accelerator supports both TCP and UDP and routes users through the AWS global network to the closest endpoint, and an NLB handles TCP and UDP traffic for the EC2 instances. ALBs don't support UDP, and CloudFront doesn't support arbitrary TCP/UDP game traffic.

Writing orders to an SQS queue decouples order intake from database writes so no orders are lost under load, and an Auto Scaling group of consumers reads from the queue and writes to Aurora at a pace the database handles. SNS can't buffer for a database endpoint, and scheduled scaling doesn't match unpredictable traffic.

Each job processes about 2 MB, needs 1 GB of memory, and finishes within 30 seconds, so a Lambda function with Python is the cheapest and starts immediately. Glue and EMR Spark are built for big data, with more startup time and cost.

Converting the Single-AZ instance to Multi-AZ by modifying it adds a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover and the same endpoint, so no code changes are needed. Restoring from a snapshot or using read replicas or Auto Scaling for the database changes the endpoint or isn't supported.

EBS Multi-Attach is supported only on Provisioned IOPS SSD io1/io2 volumes (on Nitro instances in the same AZ), so io2 meets the need for simultaneous writes from multiple instances. gp2, gp3, and st1 volumes don't support Multi-Attach.

The EC2 tier runs in a single AZ, so Multi-AZ Auto Scaling with an Application Load Balancer spreads instances across AZs and removes that single point of failure (the RDS tier is already Multi-AZ). Snapshots or Route 53 routing alone don't give high availability.

Turning on discount sharing in the Organizations management account's Billing preferences lets the Savings Plan discount apply to eligible usage in other accounts of the organization, so the unused commitment is used. Savings Plans can't be sold in the RI Marketplace, and moving workloads is more work.

A REST API in API Gateway fronts the containers, and a VPC link (private integration) lets API Gateway reach the ECS services in private subnets. WebSocket APIs are not REST, and a security group alone doesn't let API Gateway reach private resources.

The access pattern can't be predicted, so S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects automatically between access tiers to minimize cost without retrieval fees. Standard-IA lifecycle transitions penalize frequently accessed objects, and replication or inventory-based approaches are not the right tools.

An egress-only internet gateway allows outbound IPv6 traffic from instances to the internet while preventing inbound connections initiated from the internet. NAT gateways are for IPv4, and a normal internet gateway allows inbound connections.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps traffic on the AWS network (not the internet) and has no hourly or data processing charges, so it's the cheapest for 1 TB per day. Interface endpoints incur charges, and Intelligent-Tiering or Transfer Acceleration don't keep traffic private.

DAX is an in-memory cache fully compatible with the DynamoDB API, giving microsecond reads with minimal code change (just use the DAX endpoint). DynamoDB has no read replicas as described, doubling RCUs doesn't reduce latency much, and ElastiCache requires more application changes.

CloudFront caches the static files at edge locations, reducing requests to the EC2 instances and ALB and lowering data transfer and compute costs, while improving performance. ElastiCache can't be connected to an ALB, WAF doesn't cache, and a second ALB adds cost.

Transit Gateway within each Region connects the VPCs with hub-and-spoke routing, and inter-Region Transit Gateway peering connects the Regions, avoiding a full mesh of VPC peering connections and so reducing administrative effort. Direct Connect gateways and PrivateLink aren't for full VPC-to-VPC connectivity.

Amazon EFS is a highly durable shared file system with a mount target in each AZ in a Region, it works with ECS containers, and AWS Backup can copy EFS backups to another Region to meet an 8-hour RPO. FSx for Windows is SMB-only, and the other FSx options don't use per-AZ mount targets in the same way.
